verdict.rationale: Fastmail documents its own JMAP API, with a session endpoint at api.fastmail.com, API-token and OAuth/Bearer authentication, and query, fetch and send methods. An external agent can therefore read and send mail over a documented, authenticated connection. However, the evidence shows no agent-specific connector, MCP server or AI integration, and no documentation of triage or draft workflows, so the agent path depends on custom JMAP wiring. Missing for 10: a first-party agent connector or MCP server for Claude/ChatGPT, explicit documentation of draft and triage operations (e.g. mailbox moves, keywords, drafts), and hands-on corroboration of an agent completing the read-triage-draft-send loop.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an external agent — Claude, ChatGPT, or my own — can read, triage, draft, and send my email end to end through a documented connection

citations.quote: The JMAP session resource can be found at https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session
POST a `methodCalls` array. Query, fetch, and send, all in one HTTP request.
Standard OAuth 2.0 or Bearer tokens. No custom auth protocol to implement.
